rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.figure: RBA hiked to 4.85% Nov 3 (6–3); BoE Nov 5 hike to 4.00% ~94%; Fed Dec hike ~72–76%; ECB Dec ~86%; BoJ Dec ~80%; BoC Dec ~45%
rows.read: Australia raised rates overnight, but a split vote and a cautious governor suggest it may be near the top. Britain is still expected to hike on Thursday, and most other big central banks still lean toward higher rates. Currencies are moving on hints about what comes after each hike, not the hikes themselves.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: US ISM manufacturing 55.5 (fcst 54.5), production 59.0; UK factory PMI 52.8 (5-month high); euro-area factory PMI 52.7
rows.read: Factories started the autumn strongly in the US and Britain, and euro-area industry kept growing. Solid growth gives central banks room to keep raising rates, which supports the dollar and the pound. Australia is the soft spot, with a weakening job market behind its central bank’s caution.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: Brent ~$105.25 (Monday settle $104.77, −7.6%); RBA: inflation back to top of 2–3% band only by late 2027; euro-area flash inflation Nov 4: forecast 4.0%
rows.read: Cheaper oil has eased one of the main forces pushing prices up, but inflation is still well above target in most big economies. Australia’s central bank now expects inflation to stay high until late 2027. Euro-area figures on Wednesday are the week’s main inflation test.

rows.title: Risk Sentiment
rows.figure: DXY ~101.81; US limited strikes on Iranian targets (Qeshm) Nov 2; offshore yuan −0.3% after PBoC FX reserve ratio rise; USD/CHF ~0.8186
rows.read: Markets were calm but cautious before the US midterm elections. Limited US strikes on Iranian targets reminded investors that peace talks are not a deal, and a slide in AI-linked shares is still weighing on the mood. The dollar firmed slightly and the Swiss franc kept its gains as a shelter.

rows.title: Terms of Trade
rows.figure: Brent ~$105.25, WTI ~$96.93 (+0.5% in Asia); Monday settlements $104.77 / $96.46
rows.read: Oil steadied after one of its biggest one-day falls of the war. That leaves exporters like Canada with less support than a week ago and importers like Japan and the euro area with a smaller bill. A setback in talks could send prices back up fast.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: CFTC Oct 27: funds strongly against CAD, against EUR (real money for), against NZD, for AUD (real money strongly against), strongly for gold (cut); oil net long among weakest since 2015
rows.read: Hedge funds hold their biggest bets against the Canadian dollar, and they are also betting against the euro and the kiwi, while real money investors bet for the euro. Their large bets on gold are shrinking. New figures arrive Friday.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: Fitch: France A+, outlook negative (Oct 30); Moody’s Aa3 negative; French budget revenue vote Nov 3; Canada budget Nov 5, 3:00 PM CT
rows.read: France’s debt worries, with two rating firms on negative outlook, keep a weight on the euro. France’s parliament votes on the revenue side of its budget today, and Canada presents its budget on Thursday.
